ko.R: 실로의 젊은 여자들이 춤추러 나오는지 지켜보아라. 그들이 나오면 포도원에서 뛰어나가라. 저마다 실로의 젊은 여자 하나를 붙잡아 아내로 삼아라. 그리고 그 여자를 베냐민 땅으로 데려가거라.

decisions.choice: to dance in the dances: women's dancing at a festival
decisions.reason: Women danced at times of celebration, with music and singing (Exodus 15:20; Judges 11:34; 1 Samuel 18:6). At the festival the young women of Shiloh would come out into the open, away from their homes.

decisions.choice: seize: snatch, carry off by force
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a robber or a lion catching its prey (Psalm 10:9). The young women are not asked; they are carried off. Verse 23 calls it "robbing".

decisions.choice: young women of Shiloh
decisions.reason: "The daughters of" a town are its girls and young women. Balanced and Readable say so; Literal keeps "daughters".

source.text: וְהָיָ֡ה כִּֽי־יָבֹ֣אוּ אֲבוֹתָם֩ א֨וֹ אֲחֵיהֶ֜ם לָרִ֣יב׀אֵלֵ֗ינוּ וְאָמַ֤רְנוּ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ חָנּ֣וּנוּ אוֹתָ֔ם כִּ֣י לֹ֥א לָקַ֛חְנוּ אִ֥ישׁ אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה כִּ֣י לֹ֥א אַתֶּ֛ם נְתַתֶּ֥ם לָהֶ֖ם כָּעֵ֥ת תֶּאְשָֽׁמוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when come their fathers or their brothers to complain to us, then we will say to them, be gracious to us [with] them, for not we took each his wife in the battle; for not you, you gave to them; at [the] time you would be guilty.

en.L: And it will be, when their fathers or their brothers come to complain to us, that we will say to them, 'Grant them to us graciously, because we did not take a wife for each man in the battle; for you did not give [them] to them, [else] now you would be guilty.'"
en.B: When their fathers or brothers come to us to protest, we will tell them, 'Do us a kindness and let them keep the women, because we did not take a wife for each of them in the war. And since you did not give them your daughters, you are not guilty of breaking the oath.'"
en.R: If their fathers or brothers come to us to complain, we will say to them, 'Please be kind to us and let the men of Benjamin keep them. When we fought against Jabesh-gilead, we did not get enough wives for all of them. And you did not give your daughters to them, so you have not broken your oath.'"

sw.L: Na itakuwa, baba zao au ndugu zao watakapokuja kulalamika kwetu, tutawaambia, 'Tufadhilini kwa ajili yao, kwa sababu hatukumtwalia kila mtu mke wake vitani; kwa maana ninyi hamkuwapa, [la sivyo] sasa mngekuwa na hatia.'"
sw.B: Baba zao au ndugu zao watakapokuja kwetu kulalamika, tutawaambia, 'Tutendeeni wema, waacheni wawe nao, kwa sababu hatukumpatia kila mmoja wao mke katika vita. Na kwa kuwa ninyi hamkuwapa binti zenu, hamna hatia ya kuvunja kiapo.'"
sw.R: Baba zao au ndugu zao wakija kulalamika kwetu, tutawaambia, 'Tafadhali tuoneeni wema, waacheni watu wa Benyamini wakae nao. Tulipopigana na Yabeshi-gileadi, hatukupata wake wa kuwatosha wote. Nanyi hamkuwapa binti zenu, kwa hiyo hamjavunja kiapo chenu.'"

es.L: Y sucederá que, cuando sus padres o sus hermanos vengan a quejarse ante nosotros, les diremos: “{{plural_you:Concédannoslas|Concedédnoslas}} por favor, porque no tomamos mujer para cada uno en la batalla; pues no {{plural_you:se las dieron ustedes|se las disteis vosotros}}, [de lo contrario] ahora {{plural_you:serían|seríais}} culpables”».
es.B: Cuando sus padres o hermanos vengan a protestar ante nosotros, les diremos: “{{plural_you:Hágannos|Hacednos}} el favor de dejar que se queden con ellas, porque en la guerra no conseguimos una esposa para cada uno de ellos. Y como no {{plural_you:fueron ustedes|fuisteis vosotros}} quienes les dieron a sus hijas, no {{plural_you:son|sois}} culpables de romper el juramento”».
es.R: Si sus padres o hermanos vienen a quejarse ante nosotros, les diremos: “Por favor, {{plural_you:sean|sed}} buenos con nosotros y {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que los hombres de Benjamín se queden con ellas. Cuando peleamos contra Jabés de Galaad, no conseguimos esposas para todos ellos. Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no les {{plural_you:dieron|disteis}} a sus hijas, así que no {{plural_you:han roto|habéis roto}} su juramento”».

fr.L: Et il arrivera, quand leurs pères ou leurs frères viendront se plaindre à nous, que nous leur dirons : “Accordez-les-nous par grâce, car nous n’avons pas pris une femme pour chacun dans la guerre ; car ce n’est pas vous qui [les] leur avez données, [sinon] vous seriez maintenant coupables.” »
fr.B: Quand leurs pères ou leurs frères viendront se plaindre à nous, nous leur dirons : “Faites-nous cette grâce de les leur laisser, car nous n’avons pas pris une femme pour chacun d’eux à la guerre. Et puisque ce n’est pas vous qui leur avez donné vos filles, vous n’êtes pas coupables d’avoir violé le serment.” »
fr.R: Si leurs pères ou leurs frères viennent se plaindre auprès de nous, nous leur dirons : “S’il vous plaît, soyez bons envers nous, et laissez-les aux hommes de Benjamin. Quand nous avons combattu Jabesh-Galaad, nous n’avons pas trouvé assez de femmes pour eux tous. Et ce n’est pas vous qui leur avez donné vos filles, donc vous n’avez pas rompu votre serment.” »

vi.L: Khi cha hay anh em của họ đến khiếu nại với chúng tôi, chúng tôi sẽ nói với họ: 'Xin vì chúng tôi mà rộng lòng với họ, vì chúng tôi đã không lấy được vợ cho mỗi người trong trận chiến; vì các ông đã không gả [con gái] cho họ, [nếu không] thì bây giờ các ông đã mắc tội.'"
vi.B: Khi cha hay anh em của các cô ấy đến phàn nàn với chúng tôi, chúng tôi sẽ nói với họ: 'Xin làm ơn cho chúng tôi mà để họ giữ các cô ấy, vì trong cuộc chiến chúng tôi đã không lấy được vợ cho mỗi người. Và vì các ông không tự gả con gái cho họ, nên các ông không mắc tội bội lời thề.'"
vi.R: Nếu cha hay anh em của các cô ấy đến phàn nàn với chúng tôi, chúng tôi sẽ nói với họ: 'Xin rộng lòng với chúng tôi mà để những người Bên-gia-min giữ các cô ấy. Khi đánh Gia-be Ga-la-át, chúng tôi đã không có đủ vợ cho tất cả họ. Còn các ông không gả con gái mình cho họ, nên các ông không hề bội lời thề.'"

ko.L: 그 여자들의 아버지나 오라버니들이 우리에게 와서 따지면, 우리가 그들에게 말하겠다. '그들을 우리에게 은혜로 베풀어 주시오. 우리가 전쟁에서 그들 각자에게 아내를 얻어 주지 못하였소. 당신들이 [딸들을] 그들에게 준 것이 아니니, 이제 당신들에게는 죄가 없소.'"
ko.B: 그 여자들의 아버지나 오라버니들이 우리에게 와서 따지면, 우리가 그들에게 이렇게 말하겠다. '우리를 보아서 그 여자들을 그들에게 맡겨 주시오. 우리가 전쟁에서 그들 모두에게 아내를 얻어 주지 못하였소. 그리고 당신들이 딸들을 그들에게 준 것이 아니니, 맹세를 어긴 죄도 없소.'"
ko.R: 그 여자들의 아버지나 오라버니들이 와서 우리에게 따지면, 우리가 이렇게 말하겠다. '부디 우리를 보아서 베냐민 사람들이 그 여자들을 데리고 살게 해 주시오. 우리가 야베스 길르앗과 싸웠을 때 그들 모두에게 줄 아내를 얻지 못하였소. 그리고 당신들이 딸들을 그들에게 준 것이 아니니, 당신들은 맹세를 어기지 않았소.'"

decisions.choice: to complain: the word the Hebrew text tells readers to read
decisions.reason: The written letters give a different vowel pattern, which could be read as "to be many"; the marginal reading of the Masoretes, which the vowels follow, gives "to bring a complaint". Only the second makes sense here.

decisions.choice: be gracious to us with them: do us the favor of letting them be
decisions.reason: The elders ask the families to show them kindness for the young women's sake, that is, to let the marriages stand and not demand the women back.

decisions.choice: we did not take a wife for each man in the battle: the war on Jabesh-gilead did not supply enough wives
alternatives: the Benjaminites did not take them as captives of war
decisions.reason: The elders explain that the battle against Jabesh-gilead gave only 400 women for 600 men (verses 12, 14). Another reading takes "we" as speaking for the Benjaminites: they did not capture these women as spoil of war, so the matter is not one of enemies. The first fits the story of this chapter more closely.

decisions.choice: you did not give them; otherwise you would now be guilty
alternatives: "you did not give them at the time, when you would have been guilty"
decisions.reason: The families gave nothing; their daughters were taken. So they have not broken the oath of verse 1 and are not under its curse (verse 18). Had they given their daughters, they would be guilty. The plan keeps the words of the oath while the fathers lose their daughters without consent.

decisions.choice: you are not guilty of breaking the oath / you have not broken your oath
alternatives: or now you would be guilty
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what guilt is meant, following meaning decision m4, and put the clause in a positive form.

decisions.choice: When we fought against Jabesh-gilead
decisions.reason: Readable names the battle meant, following meaning decision m3. It depends on that reading.

decisions.choice: The elders speak to the fathers and brothers of Shiloh in the 하오체 with "당신들"
decisions.reason: They speak to fellow Israelites as equals in a delicate matter; the 하오체 is courteous without being humble.

source.text: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ נָשִׁים֙ לְמִסְפָּרָ֔ם מִן־הַמְּחֹלְל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּזָ֑לוּ וַיֵּלְכ֗וּ וַיָּשׁ֨וּבוּ֙ אֶל־נַ֣חֲלָתָ֔ם וַיִּבְנוּ֙ אֶת־הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ בָּהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And did so [the] sons of Benjamin, and they carried off wives according to their number from the dancing women whom they seized, and they went and they returned to their inheritance, and they rebuilt the cities, and they lived in them.

en.L: And the sons of Benjamin did so, and carried off wives according to their number from the dancers whom they had seized; and they went and returned to their inheritance, and rebuilt the cities and lived in them.
en.B: The Benjaminites did just that. They carried off as many wives as there were men, from the dancers they had seized, and went back to their own land. They rebuilt their towns and settled in them.
en.R: The men of Benjamin did what the elders said. Each man caught one of the young women who were dancing and took her as his wife. Then they went back to their own land. They rebuilt their towns and lived in them.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Benyamini wakafanya hivyo, wakajitwalia wake kwa hesabu yao kutoka katika wale wachezaji waliowanyakua; wakaenda, wakarudi katika urithi wao, wakaijenga miji upya, wakakaa ndani yake.
sw.B: Wabenyamini walifanya hivyo hivyo. Walijitwalia wake kwa idadi yao, kutoka kwa wale wachezaji waliowanyakua, wakarudi katika nchi yao wenyewe. Waliijenga miji yao upya, wakakaa humo.
sw.R: Watu wa Benyamini walifanya kama wazee walivyosema. Kila mtu alimkamata mmoja wa wasichana waliokuwa wakicheza, akamchukua kuwa mke wake. Kisha walirudi katika nchi yao wenyewe. Waliijenga miji yao upya, wakaishi humo.

es.L: Y los hijos de Benjamín lo hicieron así, y tomaron mujeres conforme a su número de entre las danzantes que arrebataron; y se fueron y volvieron a su heredad, y reedificaron las ciudades y habitaron en ellas.
es.B: Los benjamitas hicieron precisamente eso. De entre las danzantes que habían arrebatado se llevaron tantas esposas como hombres había, y regresaron a su tierra. Reconstruyeron sus ciudades y se establecieron en ellas.
es.R: Los hombres de Benjamín hicieron lo que los ancianos dijeron. Cada uno atrapó a una de las jóvenes que bailaban y la tomó por esposa. Después volvieron a su tierra. Reconstruyeron sus pueblos y vivieron en ellos.

fr.L: Et les fils de Benjamin firent ainsi, et ils enlevèrent des femmes selon leur nombre parmi les danseuses qu’ils avaient ravies ; et ils s’en allèrent et retournèrent dans leur héritage, et ils rebâtirent les villes et y habitèrent.
fr.B: Les Benjaminites firent ainsi. Ils enlevèrent parmi les danseuses autant de femmes qu’ils étaient d’hommes, et ils retournèrent dans leur héritage. Ils rebâtirent leurs villes et s’y établirent.
fr.R: Les hommes de Benjamin ont fait ce que les anciens avaient dit. Chacun a attrapé une des jeunes filles qui dansaient et l’a prise pour femme. Ensuite, ils sont retournés dans leur pays. Ils ont reconstruit leurs villes et ils y ont habité.

vi.L: Con cháu Bên-gia-min làm như vậy, và bắt vợ theo số người của mình trong những người nữ nhảy múa mà họ đã cướp; rồi họ đi trở về sản nghiệp mình, xây lại các thành và ở trong đó.
vi.B: Người Bên-gia-min làm đúng như vậy. Họ bắt đủ số vợ cho mỗi người trong những người nữ nhảy múa mà họ đã cướp, rồi trở về sản nghiệp mình. Họ xây lại các thành và định cư ở đó.
vi.R: Những người Bên-gia-min làm theo lời các trưởng lão. Mỗi người bắt một thiếu nữ đang nhảy múa và lấy nàng làm vợ. Rồi họ trở về đất của mình. Họ xây lại các thành và sống ở đó.

ko.L: 베냐민 자손이 그대로 하여, 춤추는 여자들 가운데에서 붙잡은 여자들을 자기들의 수대로 아내로 데려갔다. 그들은 자기들의 유산으로 돌아가서 성읍들을 다시 세우고 거기에서 살았다.
ko.B: 베냐민 사람들은 그대로 하였다. 그들은 춤추던 여자들 가운데에서 자기들의 수만큼 붙잡아 아내로 데려갔다. 그리고 자기들의 유산으로 돌아가 성읍들을 다시 세우고 거기에 자리 잡고 살았다.
ko.R: 베냐민 사람들은 장로들이 말한 대로 하였다. 저마다 춤추던 젊은 여자 하나를 붙잡아 아내로 삼았다. 그리고 자기들의 땅으로 돌아갔다. 그들은 성들을 다시 세우고 거기에서 살았다.

decisions.choice: seized: robbed, took by force
decisions.reason: The verb means to rob or tear away what belongs to another (Genesis 31:31; Micah 2:2). The narrator's word shows what the plan really was.

decisions.choice: according to their number: one wife for each man still without one
decisions.reason: The 400 from Jabesh-gilead had left 200 men without wives (verse 14); each of these took one of the dancers.

decisions.choice: their inheritance, the cities: Benjamin's allotted land and the towns burned in the war
decisions.reason: The inheritance is the land given to the tribe (Joshua 18:11-28). The towns had been burned by Israel's army (20:48); now they are rebuilt and the tribe lives on.

decisions.choice: their own land
decisions.reason: "Inheritance" here is the tribe's allotted land, so Balanced and Readable say "land". Readable also names the elders as the ones whose plan was carried out.

source.text: וַיִּתְהַלְּכ֨וּ מִשָּׁ֤ם בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא אִ֥ישׁ לְשִׁבְט֖וֹ וּלְמִשְׁפַּחְתּ֑וֹ וַיֵּצְא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ לְנַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And dispersed from there [the] sons of Israel at the time the that, each to his tribe and to his clan, and they went out from there each to his inheritance.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went away from there at that time, each man to his tribe and to his clan; and they went out from there, each to his inheritance.
en.B: At that time the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left that place and went home, each man to his own tribe and clan, each to his own land.
en.R: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left there. Each man went home to his own tribe and family, to the land that belonged to him.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakaondoka huko wakati huo, kila mtu kwa kabila lake na kwa ukoo wake; wakatoka huko, kila mtu kwenda urithini mwake.
sw.B: Wakati huo Waisraeli waliondoka mahali pale, wakaenda nyumbani, kila mtu kwa kabila lake na ukoo wake, kila mtu kwenye nchi yake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Kisha Waisraeli waliondoka huko. Kila mtu alirudi nyumbani kwa kabila lake na jamaa yake, kwenye nchi iliyokuwa yake.

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel se fueron de allí en aquel tiempo, cada uno a su tribu y a su clan; y salieron de allí, cada uno a su heredad.
es.B: En aquel tiempo los israelitas se fueron de allí y volvieron a sus casas, cada uno a su tribu y a su clan, cada uno a su heredad.
es.R: Después los israelitas se fueron de allí. Cada uno volvió a su casa, a su tribu y a su familia, a la tierra que le pertenecía.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël s’en allèrent de là en ce temps-là, chacun vers sa tribu et vers son clan ; et ils sortirent de là, chacun vers son héritage.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} quittèrent alors ce lieu et rentrèrent chez eux, chacun dans sa tribu et son clan, chacun dans son héritage.
fr.R: Ensuite, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} sont partis de là. Chacun est rentré chez lui, dans sa tribu et sa famille, sur la terre qui lui appartenait.

vi.L: Lúc ấy con cái Y-sơ-ra-ên rời khỏi đó, ai nấy về chi tộc và gia tộc mình; họ ra đi từ đó, ai nấy về sản nghiệp mình.
vi.B: Lúc ấy dân Y-sơ-ra-ên rời khỏi nơi đó mà về nhà, ai nấy về chi tộc và gia tộc mình, ai nấy về sản nghiệp mình.
vi.R: Rồi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên rời khỏi đó. Ai nấy về nhà mình, về với chi tộc và gia đình mình, về phần đất thuộc về mình.

ko.L: 그때 이스라엘 자손은 그곳을 떠나 저마다 자기 지파와 가문으로 갔다. 그들은 거기에서 나가 저마다 자기 유산으로 갔다.
ko.B: 그때 이스라엘 자손은 그곳을 떠나 저마다 자기 지파와 가문으로, 자기 유산으로 돌아갔다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 이스라엘 백성은 그곳을 떠났다. 저마다 자기 지파와 집안이 있는 곳, 곧 자기 땅으로 돌아갔다.

decisions.choice: each to his inheritance: the people go home, as at the end of Joshua
decisions.reason: Joshua's work ended with the people sent away, each to his inheritance (Joshua 24:28; Judges 2:6). Judges closes its own story with the same picture, but after a civil war rather than a covenant.

decisions.choice: his tribe and his clan: the larger and smaller units of Israel
decisions.reason: Each tribe was made up of clans, groups of related families (Joshua 7:14). The men return to their own people and land.

decisions.choice: each man
decisions.reason: Those who go home are the men of the assembly and the army (20:2, 17), so "man" and "his" are kept with no gender setting.

source.text: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִ֛ישׁ הַיָּשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: In the days the those there [was] no king in Israel; each the right in his eyes he did.

en.L: In those days [there was] no king in Israel; each did what [was] right in his own eyes.
en.B: In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what they thought was right.
en.R: At that time Israel had no king. Everyone did whatever seemed right to them.

sw.L: Katika siku hizo hapakuwa na mfalme katika Israeli; kila mtu alifanya yaliyo sawa machoni pake mwenyewe.
sw.B: Siku hizo hapakuwa na mfalme katika Israeli; kila mtu alifanya alivyoona ni sawa.
sw.R: Wakati huo Israeli hawakuwa na mfalme. Kila mtu alifanya lolote alilodhani ni sawa.

es.L: En aquellos días no [había] rey en Israel; cada uno hacía lo recto a sus propios ojos.
es.B: En aquellos días no había rey en Israel; cada uno hacía lo que le parecía bien.
es.R: En aquel tiempo Israel no tenía rey. Cada uno hacía lo que le parecía bien.

fr.L: En ces jours-là, [il n’y avait] pas de roi en Israël ; chacun faisait ce qui [était] droit à ses yeux.
fr.B: En ce temps-là, il n’y avait pas de roi en Israël ; chacun faisait ce qui lui semblait bon.
fr.R: À cette époque, Israël n’avait pas de roi. Chacun faisait ce qui lui paraissait bien.

decisions.choice: each did what was right in his own eyes: each person was his own standard
decisions.reason: As in 17:6. Israel was to do "what is right in the eyes of the LORD" (Deuteronomy 12:25, 28; 13:19), and Moses warned against each one doing "whatever is right in his own eyes" (Deuteronomy 12:8). This chapter shows it: oaths sworn in anger, an Israelite town destroyed, and young women carried off, all to keep the words of a vow.

decisions.choice: there was no king in Israel: the refrain that closes the book
decisions.reason: The saying first appears in full at 17:6, its first half in 18:1 and 19:1, and now it is the book's last sentence. It looks back from a time when Israel had kings and sums up the disorder of chapters 17-21. The book does not say whether a human king would solve the problem; Gideon had said that the LORD was Israel's ruler (8:23), and the request for a king in 1 Samuel 8 is told as a rejection of God's rule.

decisions.choice: everyone did what they thought was right
decisions.reason: As in 17:6: "in his own eyes" means by one's own judgment, and the saying covers all the people, so Balanced and Readable say "everyone ... they". Literal keeps the Hebrew picture.

decisions.choice: The refrain worded exactly as at 17:6
decisions.reason: The Joshua–Ruth terms note asks for the same words at 17:6 and 21:25, so the book ends on the sentence the reader has already met.
